answers.plain:
**Subject:** Snack Signup for T-Ball Season! ⚾🍎

Hi T-Ball families,

I'm so excited for the season ahead, and I'm happy to be coordinating snacks this year! Here's how it will work:

**What we need:** One family to bring a snack for the team at each game over the next 6 Saturdays. With 14 families and 6 games, not everyone will need to sign up. Each family will be asked to bring a snack no more than once.

**Important: we're keeping it nut-free.** Some of our kids have allergies, so please avoid anything that contains nuts or peanuts, or that is made in a facility with them. Please check labels carefully. Some good ideas include:

- Fruit slices, grapes, or orange wedges
- Goldfish crackers or pretzels (check the label)
- Cheese sticks
- Juice boxes or water
- Fruit snacks or granola bars labeled nut-free

**How to sign up:** Just reply to this email with the Saturday you'd like, and I'll confirm your spot. Dates are first come, first served. If you'd rather I use a shared sheet, let me know and I'll set one up.

Please bring enough for the whole team (about 12 kids plus siblings if you're feeling generous!). Individually wrapped items make for easy handouts.

Thank you all for helping make this season fun for the kids. If you have any questions or concerns about allergies, please reach out anytime.

Go team! 🧢

[Your name]
Snack Coordinator

---

A few things to fill in or adjust:
- **Dates:** I left out specific dates, so you may want to list the 6 Saturdays.
- **Team size:** I guessed about 12 kids. Please update that to the real number.
- **Signup method:** I assumed reply-by-email. I can rewrite it for a Google Sheet or SignUpGenius link if you prefer.

**Subject:** T-Ball Snack Signup: 6 Saturdays, Nut-Free 🍎⚾

Hi T-Ball families,

Snack time is a highlight of the season for the kids, so I'm putting together the snack schedule for the next 6 Saturday games.

**What we need:** One family to bring one snack per game. There are 6 games and 14 of us, so each family will take at most one turn, and some may not be needed at all.

**The games:**
- Sat, Oct 31
- Sat, Nov 7
- Sat, Nov 14
- Sat, Nov 21
- Sat, Nov 28
- Sat, Dec 5

**To claim a date:** Reply to this email with your first-choice date and a backup. I'll confirm in a follow-up so nobody doubles up. Slots go first come, first served.

**We're keeping it nut-free.** Please don't bring anything containing peanuts or tree nuts, or anything made in a facility with them. Labels often say "may contain nuts" or "processed in a facility that also processes nuts." Please skip those. Also check granola bars, trail mix, and baked goods, since nuts are often hiding in them.

**Easy snack ideas:**
- Orange slices, apple slices, or grapes (cut in half for the littlest players)
- Clementines or bananas
- Cheese sticks or string cheese
- Pretzels, Goldfish, or animal crackers (check the label)
- Fruit pouches or applesauce cups
- Individual water bottles or juice boxes

**A few tips:**
- Individually wrapped or pre-portioned items are easiest to hand out.
- Please bring enough for about 12 kids, plus a few extras for siblings.
- Please bring the snack to the field by the end of the game, and have a dozen or so napkins or wipes on hand if you can.

If your child has a food allergy or dietary need besides nuts, such as dairy, gluten, or egg, please let me know privately. I'll make sure the whole team's snacks work for everyone.

Thanks so much for helping. The kids will love it, and I'm looking forward to a fun season!

Best,
[Your name]
[Phone number]
Snack Coordinator, [Team name]

---

Optional tweaks:
- **Reply deadline:** Add one, like "Please reply by Friday," so you aren't chasing people.
- **Shared sheet:** A Google Sheet or SignUpGenius link lets families see open dates themselves. It's less back-and-forth for you than email replies. I can write a short version of this email around the link.
- **Two families per game:** With 14 families you could do two per game (12 slots, 2 spare). Each family would then bring half as much, which many parents prefer.
- **Halloween:** Oct 31 is Halloween. If the kids will be in costume, you could mention it, and families may want to skip candy that day.

Want me to make it shorter, funnier, or more formal?
